title: Revisiting What Happened to Anita Hill

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收看《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片时代，当我在夜总会当DJ时，每晚你都要带着300张你最珍爱的宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个像是由50年前精美老物件组成的流动的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在，请在您喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: 27 years ago, the Senate Judiciary Committee interrogated Anita Hill and Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 27年前，参议院司法委员会对安妮塔·希尔和克拉伦斯·托马斯进行了质询。

sentences.en: How what happened then is shaping what happens tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 当时的往事如何塑造着未来的走向。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, September 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月26日，星期三。

sentences.en: A little bit more about what went into your decision to resign at this time and what the motivations were.
sentences.zh: 关于你决定在此时辞职的前因后果以及你的动机，能再多谈谈吗？

sentences.en: You mentioned your doctor and your wife.
sentences.zh: 你提到了你的医生和你的妻子。

sentences.en: Well, I looked at the facts and the law and put them together and came out with an opinion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我研究了事实和法律，把它们结合起来，然后得出了一种观点。

sentences.en: Justice Marshall, would you share with us some of the medical facts?
sentences.zh: 马歇尔大法官，你能和我们分享一些医疗方面的事实吗？

sentences.en: What's wrong with you, sir?
sentences.zh: 先生，你怎么了？

sentences.en: What's wrong with me?
sentences.zh: 我怎么了？

sentences.en: I'm old.
sentences.zh: 我老了。

sentences.en: The story of the Clarence Thomas-Anita Hill confrontation starts in July of 1991 when Supreme Court Justice Thurgood Marshall announced his retirement.
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·托马斯与安妮塔·希尔对抗的故事始于1991年7月，当时最高法院大法官瑟古德·马歇尔宣布退休。

sentences.en: I have followed this man's career for some time, and he has excelled in everything that he has attempted.
sentences.zh: 我关注这个人的职业生涯有一段时间了，他尝试过的每件事都极其出色。

sentences.en: President George H.W.
sentences.zh: 老乔治·H·W·

sentences.en: Bush, the first Bush, nominated Clarence Thomas, a conservative judge, to replace him.
sentences.zh: 布什，也就是老布什，提名保守派法官克拉伦斯·托马斯来接替他。

sentences.en: And I trust that the Senate will confirm this able man promptly.
sentences.zh: 我信任参议院会迅速确认这位能干的人。

sentences.en: Keith Zernicke covers politics for The Times.
sentences.zh: 基思·泽尔尼克为《时报》报道政治新闻。

sentences.en: The hearings start in September.
sentences.zh: 听证会于9月开始。

sentences.en: The hearing will come to order.
sentences.zh: 听证会现在开始。

sentences.en: There are questions about Clarence Thomas' fairly conservative legal record, but that's not a surprise to the senators who are asking questions.
sentences.zh: 人们对克拉伦斯·托马斯相当保守的法律记录存在疑问，但这对于提问的参议员来说并不意外。

sentences.en: So it looks as if this is probably going to be a fairly straightforward confirmation.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来这可能将是一次相当直接的确认。

sentences.en: But meanwhile, there's a parallel story developing.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，一个平行的故事正在展开。

sentences.en: There are these rumors out there that Clarence Thomas had sexually harassed women in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 有传言称克拉伦斯·托马斯在职场中对女性进行性骚扰。

sentences.en: So Senate staffers are sort of looking behind the scenes, trying to figure out who this is, and they get a lead on one woman, and her name is Anita Hill.
sentences.zh: 因此参议院工作人员在幕后进行调查，试图弄清楚这个人是谁，他们获得了一条线索，指向了一位名叫安妮塔·希尔的女性。

sentences.en: So right before the hearings start, the Democrats call Anita Hill.
sentences.zh: 就在听证会开始前，民主党人找到了安妮塔·希尔。

sentences.en: And Anita Hill is willing to tell her story, but she's not sure that she wants to use her name or come forward publicly.
sentences.zh: 安妮塔·希尔愿意讲述她的故事，但她不确定自己是否愿意公开姓名或站出来。

sentences.en: The Democrats tell her she has to give her name at least to the Senate Judiciary Committee members, and the nominee, Clarence Thomas, has to know her name.
sentences.zh: 民主党人告诉她，她必须把名字至少告诉参议院司法委员会成员，而且被提名人克拉伦斯·托马斯也必须知道她的名字。

sentences.en: Anita Hill agrees that her name can be passed on to the Judiciary Committee and to the nominee, Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 安妮塔·希尔同意将她的名字转交给司法委员会和被提名人克拉伦斯·托马斯。

sentences.en: She writes a sworn affidavit about her allegations, and the White House was willing to investigate this.
sentences.zh: 她就自己的指控写了一份宣誓书，白宫愿意对此进行调查。

sentences.en: The White House was willing to say, OK, we'll look into this.
sentences.zh: 白宫愿意表示，好吧，我们会调查这件事。

sentences.en: I think they understood that they could not just brush this woman away.
sentences.zh: 我想他们明白，他们不能就这样把这个女人打发走。

sentences.en: The White House looks it over, decides pretty quickly, there's nothing here, this is unfounded.
sentences.zh: 白宫审阅了这份材料，很快得出结论：这里没什么东西，这是毫无根据的。

sentences.en: They pass it along to Thomas.
sentences.zh: 他们把这份材料转交给了托马斯。

sentences.en: Thomas writes a statement saying this is completely false.
sentences.zh: 托马斯写了一份声明，称这完全是捏造。

sentences.en: But keep in mind, this is all happening behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，这一切都是在幕后发生的。

sentences.en: This is the White House, the Senate Judiciary Committee, Anita Hill, Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 涉及的有白宫、参议院司法委员会、安妮塔·希尔和克拉伦斯·托马斯。

sentences.en: The public has no idea this is happening.
sentences.zh: 公众对这一切一无所知。

sentences.en: Thank you all very, very much.
sentences.zh: 非常非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: So at this point, Clarence Thomas' hearings are over, and it looks like the nomination is going to sail through.
sentences.zh: 所以到目前为止，克拉伦斯·托马斯的听证会已经结束，看来提名将顺利通过。

sentences.en: Ms. Yard, I hope I get to see you next August, but I hope it's not at one of these hearings.
sentences.zh: 亚德女士，我希望明年八月还能见到你，但我希望不是在这样的听证会上。

sentences.en: But the full Senate has yet to take a vote on its nomination.
sentences.zh: 但全体参议院尚未对他的提名进行投票。

sentences.en: This is Weekend Edition.
sentences.zh: 这里是《周末版》。

sentences.en: I'm Leanne Hanson.
sentences.zh: 我是莉安·汉森。

sentences.en: Then the story leaks.
sentences.zh: 接着，消息泄露了。

sentences.en: A woman who served as personal assistant to Clarence Thomas for over two years has accused him of sexually harassing her.
sentences.zh: 一名曾担任克拉伦斯·托马斯私人助理两年多的女性指控他对其进行性骚扰。

sentences.en: On October 6th, NPR and Newsday break the story.
sentences.zh: 10月6日，美国国家公共广播电台和《新闻日报》爆出了这则新闻。

sentences.en: According to Hill's affidavit, Thomas, after a brief work discussion, would, quote, turn conversation to discussions about his sexual interests.
sentences.zh: 根据希尔的宣誓书，托马斯在一次简短的工作讨论后，会，引述，“把谈话转向关于他性趣的话题”。

sentences.en: So suddenly, Anita Hill's name is public.
sentences.zh: 于是突然之间，安妮塔·希尔的名字公开了。

sentences.en: There's much demand to hear more from Anita Hill.
sentences.zh: 各方强烈要求听到安妮塔·希尔更多的说法。

sentences.en: The first point that I want to address with you is the idea that this is somehow a political ploy that I am involved in.
sentences.zh: 我要向大家阐明的第一个观点是，这不知怎么成了我参与其中的一个政治诡计。

sentences.en: After the story breaks, she gives a press conference.
sentences.zh: 在这则新闻爆出后，她举行了一场记者招待会。

sentences.en: Nothing could be further from the truth.
sentences.zh: 事实远非如此。

sentences.en: The Senate Judiciary Committee realizes it's got a problem.
sentences.zh: 参议院司法委员会意识到它遇到了麻烦。

sentences.en: We ought to take another day or two to look at this thing and make sure we're doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: 我们应该再花一两天时间来看看这件事，确保我们做的是正确的事。

sentences.en: It hardly is asking too much that we delay a brief time to more thoroughly investigate this.
sentences.zh: 要求推迟一小段时间以便更彻底地调查此事，实在算不上过分的要求。

sentences.en: They delay the vote of the full Senate.
sentences.zh: 他们推迟了全体参议院的投票。

sentences.en: They reopen the hearings.
sentences.zh: 他们重新召开了听证会。

sentences.en: And Anita Hill is going to tell her story under oath before the Senate Judiciary Committee the next week.
sentences.zh: 安妮塔·希尔将于第二周在参议院司法委员会面前宣誓讲述她的故事。

sentences.en: A majority of Americans in a poll released today say that they are not inclined to believe the charges against Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 在今天公布的一项民意调查中，多数美国人表示他们倾向于不相信针对克拉伦斯·托马斯的指控。

sentences.en: The first reaction is that there's a lot of doubt about Anita Hill's story.
sentences.zh: 最初的反应是，对安妮塔·希尔的故事存在很多怀疑。

sentences.en: Professor Hill's allegations and credibility are the topic of much debate throughout.
sentences.zh: 希尔教授的指控和信誉是各方广泛争论的话题。

sentences.en: People wondered why she hadn't come forward sooner.
sentences.zh: 人们想知道为什么她没有早点站出来。

sentences.en: They wondered why she'd followed him from one job to another if he was really sexually harassing her.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道，如果他真的在性骚扰她，她为什么还要跟着他从一个工作换到另一个工作。

sentences.en: And the whole concept of sexual harassment in the workplace, the country hadn't struggled with this.
sentences.zh: 整个职场性骚扰的概念，这个国家此前并未真正为此挣扎过。

sentences.en: We hadn't figured out what it looked like.
sentences.zh: 我们还没弄清楚它到底是什么样子的。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people thought it was kind of a bogus thing.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人认为这是一种虚假的东西。

sentences.en: It didn't really happen.
sentences.zh: 这并没有真正发生。

sentences.en: And to have a 10-year-old allegation come in here now and try to blow him out of the water
sentences.zh: 现在突然冒出一个十年前的指控，想要彻底击垮他，

sentences.en: on the weekend before the final vote
sentences.zh: 就在最后一次投票前的那个周末，

sentences.en: in an October last-ditch, last-second political surprise
sentences.zh: 这是十月里最后关头的孤注一掷、最后一秒的政治偷袭，

sentences.en: I think is reprehensible.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是极其可耻的。

sentences.en: From CBS News headquarters in New York, here is Dan Rather.
sentences.zh: 来自纽约的哥伦比亚广播公司新闻总部，我是丹·拉瑟。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Drama and history on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 国会山正在上演充满戏剧性和历史性的一幕。

sentences.en: The United States Senate Judiciary Committee is about to begin an unprecedented hearing.
sentences.zh: 美国参议院司法委员会即将开始一场前所未有的听证会。

sentences.en: The hearing day comes October 11th.
sentences.zh: 听证会的那天是10月11日。

sentences.en: And it is a Washington spectacle, it is a national spectacle.
sentences.zh: 这是一场华盛顿的奇观，也是一场全国的奇观。

sentences.en: It's credited with photographers, television cameras, there are lights on the nominee.
sentences.zh: 这里挤满了摄影师、电视摄像机，聚光灯都打在被提名人身上。

sentences.en: The panel of senators all take their place.
sentences.zh: 参议员评审团全体就座。

sentences.en: Joe Biden, who's the committee's chairman and a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登，委员会主席，也是一名民主党人。

sentences.en: The hearing will come to order.
sentences.zh: 听证会现在开始。

sentences.en: Gavels open the hearing.
sentences.zh: 法槌敲响，听证会开幕。

sentences.en: Achieving fairness in the atmosphere in which these hearings are being held.
sentences.zh: 要在这些听证会召开的氛围中实现公正。

sentences.en: And makes a statement talking about what a difficult day it is.
sentences.zh: 并发表声明，谈到这是多么艰难的一天。

sentences.en: May be the most difficult task at least I have ever undertaken in my close to 19 years in the United States Senate.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我在美国参议院近19年的时间里承担过的最艰难的任务，至少也是之一。

sentences.en: And then they turn the microphone over to the nominee, to Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把话筒交给被提名人，交给克拉伦斯·托马斯。

sentences.en: You have an opening statement, please proceed.
sentences.zh: 你有一份开场陈述，请继续。

sentences.en: Mr. Chairman, Senator Thurman, members of the committee.
sentences.zh: 主席先生，瑟蒙德参议员，委员会成员们。

sentences.en: Clarence Thomas makes a very brief opening statement.
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·托马斯作了一份非常简短的开场陈述。

sentences.en: As excruciatingly difficult as the last two weeks have been.
sentences.zh: 尽管过去两周极其痛苦难熬。

sentences.en: I welcome the opportunity to clear my name today.
sentences.zh: 我欢迎今天这个洗清我名白的机会。

sentences.en: And in that statement, he all but denies knowing Anita Hill.
sentences.zh: 在那份声明中，他几乎否认认识安妮塔·希尔。

sentences.en: Contrary to some press reports, I categorically denied all of the allegations and denied that I ever attempted to date Anita Hill.
sentences.zh: 与一些新闻报道相反，我绝对否认所有这些指控，并否认我曾试图约会安妮塔·希尔。

sentences.en: He talks about how he can't sleep.
sentences.zh: 他谈到自己如何失眠。

sentences.en: He just wants to clear his name.
sentences.zh: 他只想洗清自己的名声。

sentences.en: Yesterday, I called my mother.
sentences.zh: 昨天，我给母亲打了电话。

sentences.en: She was confined to her bed, unable to work, and unable to stop crying.
sentences.zh: 她卧床不起，无法工作，也止不住地哭泣。

sentences.en: His wife, Ginny, is sitting behind him.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子金妮坐在他身后。

sentences.en: Her chin is quivering.
sentences.zh: 她的下巴在颤抖。

sentences.en: And the picture that everyone at home watching on their television and the picture that the senators see is these allegations have undone Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 所有在家看电视的观众以及参议员们看到的画面是，这些指控已经彻底毁掉了克拉伦斯·托马斯。

sentences.en: And there's this initial sense, at least, that this is unfair to Clarence Thomas, that this good man is being taken down.
sentences.zh: 至少最初有一种感觉，即这对克拉伦斯·托马斯是不公平的，这位好人正在被拉下马。

sentences.en: Enough is enough.
sentences.zh: 够了够了。

sentences.en: The Senate's in recess.
sentences.zh: 参议院休会。

sentences.en: The hearing is in recess for five minutes.
sentences.zh: 听证会休会五分钟。

sentences.en: And then Clarence Thomas gets up and leaves the room.
sentences.zh: 然后克拉伦斯·托马斯起身离开房间。

sentences.en: I'm told security is clearing the hall.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我保安正在清场。

sentences.en: She's in the hall so that she can come down.
sentences.zh: 她在走廊里，这样她就可以走下来了。

sentences.en: Then Anita Hill comes in the room.
sentences.zh: 接着安妮塔·希尔走进了房间。

sentences.en: Welcome, Professor Hill.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，希尔教授。

sentences.en: She's wearing this electric blue suit.
sentences.zh: 她穿着这套电蓝色套装。

sentences.en: She looks very much a professional woman of that era.
sentences.zh: 她看起来非常像那个时代的职业女性。

sentences.en: And I think that image of her really sticks with people, particularly with working women who might have experienced something like what she's talking about in their own workplaces.
sentences.zh: 我想她的那个形象真的深深印在人们脑海里，特别是那些在自己的工作场所可能经历过类似她所谈论的事情的职场女性。

sentences.en: Professor Hill, please make whatever statement you would wish to make to the committee.
sentences.zh: 希尔教授，请向委员会发表你想发表的任何陈述。

sentences.en: So here she is, seated at this table, a black professional woman.
sentences.zh: 于是她坐在了这张桌子旁，一位黑人职业女性。

sentences.en: And she looks up, and what she sees is an all-male, all-white panel of Senate Judiciary Committee members.
sentences.zh: 她抬起头，看到的是一个全是由男性、全是由白人组成的参议院司法委员会成员小组。

sentences.en: Mr. Chairman, Senator Thurman, members of the committee, my name is Anita F.
sentences.zh: 主席先生，瑟蒙德参议员，委员会成员们，我的名字是安妮塔·F·

sentences.en: Hill, and I am a professor of law at the University of Oklahoma.
sentences.zh: 希尔，我是俄克拉荷马大学的法律教授。

sentences.en: She gives a brief opening statement.
sentences.zh: 她发表了简短的开场陈述。

sentences.en: She's very careful.
sentences.zh: 她非常谨慎。

sentences.en: She sticks to what she's reading in front of her.
sentences.zh: 她紧盯着她面前阅读的内容。

sentences.en: After a brief discussion of work, he would turn the conversation to a discussion of sexual matters.
sentences.zh: 在简短的工作讨论后，他会把谈话转向关于性方面话题的讨论。

sentences.en: She details the allegations.
sentences.zh: 她详细陈述了这些指控。

sentences.en: His conversations were very vivid.
sentences.zh: 他的谈话非常生动。

sentences.en: He spoke about acts that he had seen in pornographic films involving such matters as women having sex with animals and films showing group sex or rape scenes.
sentences.zh: 他谈到他在色情电影中看到的行为，涉及诸如女性与动物发生性关系的事务，以及播放群交或强奸场景的电影。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: The microphone goes back to the senators, and they begin grilling her.
sentences.zh: 话筒又回到了参议员手中，他们开始对她进行严厉盘问。

sentences.en: And what was that incident again?
sentences.zh: 那个事件到底是什么来着？

sentences.en: The incident with regard to the Coke can that's spelled out in my statement.
sentences.zh: 关于可口可乐罐的那个事件，我的声明里已经详细说明了。

sentences.en: Once again for me, please.
sentences.zh: 请再为我讲一遍。

sentences.en: The incident involved his going to his desk, getting up from a work table, going to his desk, looking at this can and saying, who put pubic hair on my Coke?
sentences.zh: 这个事件涉及他走到自己的办公桌前，从工作桌旁站起来，走到办公桌前，看着这个罐子说，谁把阴毛弄到我的可乐上了？

sentences.en: Was anyone else in his office at the time?
sentences.zh: 当时他的办公室里还有其他人吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: It's almost like the more composed Anita Hill remains, the more these senators come after her.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像是安妮塔·希尔表现得越镇定，这些参议员就越对她穷追猛打。

sentences.en: You testified this morning in response to Senator Biden that the most embarrassing question involved, this is not too bad, women's large breasts.
sentences.zh: 你今天上午在回答拜登参议员时作证说，最令人尴尬的问题涉及，这个倒还不太糟糕，女性丰满的胸部。

sentences.en: That's a word we use all the time.
sentences.zh: 那是我们经常用的一个词。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: The most embarrassing aspect was his description of the acts of these individuals.
sentences.zh: 最令人尴尬的方面是他对这些个人行为的描述。

sentences.en: And they want her to go over these graphic details again and again.
sentences.zh: 他们希望她一遍又一遍地复述这些大尺度的细节。

sentences.en: Well, in your statement to the FBI, you did refer to the films,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在给联邦调查局的陈述中，你确实提到了那些电影，

sentences.en: but there's no reference to the physical characteristic you described.
sentences.zh: 但其中没有提到你所描述的身体特征。

sentences.en: I don't want to attach too much weight to it, but I had thought you said that the aspect of the large breasts was the aspect that concerned you,
sentences.zh: 我不想过分强调这一点，但我曾以为你说过，大胸部这一方面是你所关心的方面，

sentences.en: and that was missing from the statement to the FBI.
sentences.zh: 而给联邦调查局的陈述中漏掉了这一点。

sentences.en: Then I have been misunderstood.
sentences.zh: 那是我被误解了。

sentences.en: It's clear, as this hearing goes on, that the senators see Clarence Thomas as this man of rectitude whose reputation is being ruined.
sentences.zh: 很明显，随着听证会的进行，参议员们将克拉伦斯·托马斯视为一个正直的人，而他的名誉正在被毁掉。

sentences.en: They're not really sure about Anita Hill, and in fact, they probably don't believe her.
sentences.zh: 他们对安妮塔·希尔并不十分确定，事实上，他们可能并不相信她。

sentences.en: Now, in trying to determine whether you are telling falsehoods or not,
sentences.zh: 那么，为了确定你是否在说谎，

sentences.en: I've got to determine what your motivation might be.
sentences.zh: 我必须弄清楚你的动机可能是什么。

sentences.en: Finally, the senators are done with Anita Hill.
sentences.zh: 最后，参议员们结束了对安妮塔·希尔的讯问。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: She gets up.
sentences.zh: 她站起身来。

sentences.en: She leaves, followed by this swarm of cameras that's been trained on her all day.
sentences.zh: 她离开了，身后跟着蜂拥而至的摄像机，这些摄像机一整天都对准了她。

sentences.en: But the room is still in chaos.
sentences.zh: 但房间里仍然一片混乱。

sentences.en: The committee will please come to order.
sentences.zh: 请委员会保持肃静。

sentences.en: And into that chaos walks Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·托马斯走进了这片混乱之中。

sentences.en: Judge, it's a tough day and tough night for you, I know.
sentences.zh: 法官阁下，我知道对你来说这是艰难的一天和艰难的一晚。

sentences.en: And Biden asks Thomas if he'd like to say anything.
sentences.zh: 拜登问托马斯是否想说点什么。

sentences.en: Do you have anything you'd like to say?
sentences.zh: 你有什么想说的吗？

sentences.en: The camera's swinging back to Thomas, and you can just see he is seething.
sentences.zh: 镜头转向托马斯，你能看出他正在怒火中烧。

sentences.en: He is so angry.
sentences.zh: 他太生气了。

sentences.en: It's like he's sweating anger.
sentences.zh: 感觉他连汗水里都透着愤怒。

sentences.en: This today is a travesty.
sentences.zh: 今天的这一切简直是一场闹剧。

sentences.en: I think that it is disgusting.
sentences.zh: 我认为这令人作呕。

sentences.en: And he lays into the Senate panel.
sentences.zh: 他开始猛烈抨击参议院小组。

sentences.en: And how many members of this committee would like to have the same scurrilous, uncorroborated allegations made about him?
sentences.zh: 这个委员会里有多少成员愿意让别人对他们做出同样恶毒、未经证实的主张？

sentences.en: If up until now, this whole hearing has been about sex?
sentences.zh: 如果直到现在，这场听证会的焦点一直都是性吗？

sentences.en: And from my standpoint, as a Black American, as far as I'm concerned, it is a high-tech lynching for uppity Blacks who in any way deign to think for themselves.
sentences.zh: 从我作为一名美国黑人的立场来看，就我而言，这是一场高科技的林奇私刑，针对的是那些胆敢独立思考的傲慢黑人。

sentences.en: Now, Clarence Thomas is making this about race.
sentences.zh: 现在，克拉伦斯·托马斯把这上升到了种族问题。

sentences.en: You will be lynched, destroyed, caricatured by a committee of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你们会被美国参议院委员会处以林奇私刑、毁掉名誉、刻意丑化，

sentences.en: Senate rather than hung from a tree.
sentences.zh: 而不是被吊死在树上。

sentences.en: If it was uncomfortable in the room for Anita Hill, it is incredibly tense and uncomfortable now.
sentences.zh: 如果说安妮塔·希尔在房间里感到不自在，那么现在气氛则是无比的紧张和尴尬。

sentences.en: Maybe for Clarence Thomas, but definitely for this, again, this panel of all white senators.
sentences.zh: 也许对克拉伦斯·托马斯来说是这样，但对这个由清一色白人参议员组成的委员会来说，绝对更是如此。

sentences.en: They're shrinking in their seats.
sentences.zh: 他们吓得在座位上缩成一团。

sentences.en: They're cringing.
sentences.zh: 他们感到畏缩。

sentences.en: They are so shamed.
sentences.zh: 他们感到如此羞耻。

sentences.en: They're so chastised about this.
sentences.zh: 他们为此感到如此严厉的谴责。

sentences.en: As I understand it, it was...
sentences.zh: 据我了解，当时是……

sentences.en: And if they were inclined to push back on him, he's just delegitimized that whole thing.
sentences.zh: 如果他们原本倾向于反击他，他这么一搞就彻底剥夺了他们反击的合法性。

sentences.en: I look forward to questioning again tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我期待明天继续提问。

sentences.en: And we wish you a good night's reSt.
sentences.zh: 我们祝你今晚休息好。

sentences.en: And we look forward to seeing you.
sentences.zh: 我们期待见到你。

sentences.en: So, the first day of hearings wraps up.
sentences.zh: 就这样，第一天的听证会结束了。

sentences.en: You come back the next day, and the Senate Judiciary Committee is set to begin questioning Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 你第二天回来，参议院司法委员会准备开始对克拉伦斯·托马斯进行质询。

sentences.en: And as the questions begin, it's pretty clear that the senators are going to defer to Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 随着质询的开始，很明显参议员们会对克拉伦斯·托马斯客客气气。

sentences.en: And again, I go back to the point that you've made time and again, and admirably, that you had not second-guessed the professor's credibility until now.
sentences.zh: 再次回到你多次表达过的一个观点，你非常令人钦佩地指出，直到现在你才开始质疑这位教授的可信度。

sentences.en: It came as a shock to you, as you stated.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这让你感到震惊。

sentences.en: At one point, Senator Orrin Hatch, who's a Republican from Utah, holds up a copy of The ExorciSt.
sentences.zh: 有一次，来自犹他州的共和党参议员奥林·哈atch拿出一本《驱魔人》。

sentences.en: Have you read this book?
sentences.zh: 你读过这本书吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: The Exorcist?
sentences.zh: 《驱魔人》？

sentences.en: No, Senator.
sentences.zh: 没有，参议员。

sentences.en: And says, isn't it possible that Anita Hill got the story of the pubic hair from The Exorcist?
sentences.zh: 并且说，安妮塔·希尔有没有可能是从《驱魔人》里听来的阴毛的故事？

sentences.en: In The Exorcist, there's a pubic hair in a gin glass.
sentences.zh: 在《驱魔人》里，有一个金酒杯里有阴毛的情节。

sentences.en: It's not in a Coke can.
sentences.zh: 不是在可口可乐罐里。

sentences.en: Alien pubic hair floating around in my gin.
sentences.zh: 外星人的阴毛在我的金酒里漂浮。

sentences.en: But of course, the implication is that she's piped this whole thing.
sentences.zh: 但当然，其暗示的意思是这一切都是她凭空捏造的。

sentences.en: And that for whatever reason, and we don't get to that reason,
sentences.zh: 不管出于什么原因——我们还没弄清那个原因——

sentences.en: she's just making all this up and she's come forward to tear down this tremendously honorable man who's now speaking before these senators.
sentences.zh: 她完全是在胡编乱造，她站出来是为了打倒这位现在正在这些参议员面前发言的极其尊贵的人。

sentences.en: She would have us believe that you were saying these things because you wanted to date her?
sentences.zh: 她让我们相信你之所以说这些话是因为你想和她约会？

sentences.en: It's pretty clear that this has become a he said, she said situation and that the senators, at least, believe that Clarence Thomas has the stronger story.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这已经变成了一场各执一词的局面，而且至少参议员们相信克拉伦斯·托马斯的话更有说服力。

sentences.en: Isn't a woman alive that would take the questions you've had to take and be just repelled by it?
sentences.zh: 天下难道有哪个女人会经受你所经受的那些质问，并且仅仅对此感到反感吗？

sentences.en: That's where the watershed is here.
sentences.zh: 这才是分水岭所在。

sentences.en: It is a good thing that this awareness goes up.
sentences.zh: 这种觉醒意识的提升是一件好事。

sentences.en: It is a terrible, tragic thing that it should bruise you.
sentences.zh: 而它竟然伤害了你，则是一件可怕且悲惨的事情。

sentences.en: Judge Thomas, I went through that in some detail because it is my legal judgment that the testimony of Professor Hill in the morning was flat out perjury.
sentences.zh: 托马斯法官，我之所以详细过问这些，是因为从法律判断来看，希尔教授上午的证词纯属作伪证。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: So we will reconvene tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 所以我们明天再开会。

sentences.en: There's a third day of hearings.
sentences.zh: 还有第三天的听证会。

sentences.en: They call some other witnesses.
sentences.zh: 他们传唤了一些其他证人。

sentences.en: One of them talks about Anita Hill has a condition.
sentences.zh: 其中一人谈到安妮塔·希尔有一种病症。

sentences.en: This is erotomania on her part.
sentences.zh: 这是她患有的情色妄想症。

sentences.en: My instant reaction was that this was unbelievable, preposterous.
sentences.zh: 我的第一反应是这简直难以置信、荒谬绝伦。

sentences.en: And then I said it must be a product of fantasy.
sentences.zh: 然后我说这一定是幻想的产物。

sentences.en: If you just knew these people and knew Clarence Thomas, you would know that that couldn't possibly have been true.
sentences.zh: 如果你只要了解这些人并了解克拉伦斯·托马斯，你就会知道这绝对不可能是真的。

sentences.en: Hill's lawyers introduced that she's taken a polygraph teSt.
sentences.zh: 希尔的律师提出她已经接受了测谎仪测试。

sentences.en: She's passed it.
sentences.zh: 她通过了测试。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, it comes out that there are other women who can make similar allegations against Clarence Thomas about sexual harassment in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，有消息爆出，还有其他女性可以对克拉伦斯·托马斯提出类似的关于职场性骚扰的指控。

sentences.en: These women are waiting in the wings, ready to tell their stories.
sentences.zh: 这些女性正在侧翼等待，准备讲述她们的故事。

sentences.en: But Joe Biden, the chairman, basically says, we've run out of time.
sentences.zh: 但委员会主席乔·拜登基本上说，我们的时间用完了。

sentences.en: This entire proceeding is ended.
sentences.zh: 整个诉讼程序到此结束。

sentences.en: And he gavels it to a close.
sentences.zh: 他敲下法槌宣布闭会。

sentences.en: Outside the hearing room, away from Washington, the whole country is watching this on their TV screens.
sentences.zh: 在听证室外，远离华盛顿，整个国家都在电视屏幕上看着这一切。

sentences.en: Will sexual harassment charges derail the Clarence Thomas Supreme Court nomination?
sentences.zh: 性骚扰指控会破坏克拉伦斯·托马斯提名为最高法院大法官的进程吗？

sentences.en: And it's dividing the country.
sentences.zh: 这正在使国家分裂。

sentences.en: I think the American taxpayer is damn sick and tired of this kind of a nomination process.
sentences.zh: 我认为美国纳税人对这种提名程序已经感到深恶痛绝。

sentences.en: Well, I think they're very tired of listening to the nominee do absolutely nothing but questions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他们已经厌倦了听这位被提名者除了反问什么都不做。

sentences.en: It's just the way Thurgood Marshall.
sentences.zh: 这就像瑟古德·马歇尔一样。

sentences.en: It's black versus white.
sentences.zh: 这是黑人与白人的对立。

sentences.en: It's men versus women.
sentences.zh: 这是男人与女人的对立。

sentences.en: It's a younger generation of women versus an older generation of women.
sentences.zh: 这是年轻一代女性与年长一代女性的对立。

sentences.en: There are all these dynamics of race and sex swirling.
sentences.zh: 所有这些种族和性别的动态都在盘根错节地交织着。

sentences.en: It's not as if I'm accusing you of robbing my house where I can show you evidence of wrongdoing.
sentences.zh: 这不像是我指控你抢劫我的房子，我可以向你出示不当行为的证据。

sentences.en: And that's part of the problem with the whole area of sexual harassment law, which I think, frankly, is pure mush.
sentences.zh: 这也是整个性骚扰法律领域的问题所在，坦率地说，我认为它完全是一团浆糊。

sentences.en: There's a lot of debate and certainly a lot of people on her side.
sentences.zh: 有很多辩论，而且当然有很多人站在她这一边。

sentences.en: But I think in the end, there was a sense that public opinion had shut Anita Hill out in the cold.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最后人们有一种感觉，即公众舆论把安妮塔·希尔冷落在一边。

sentences.en: And after the hearings with the Judiciary Committee, the full Senate reconvenes to vote on Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 在司法委员会的听证会之后，全体参议员重新开会，对克拉伦斯·托马斯进行投票。

sentences.en: Mr. Cochran.
sentences.zh: 科克伦先生。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 赞成。

sentences.en: Mr. Cohen.
sentences.zh: 科恩先生。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 赞成。

sentences.en: It's a very tight vote.
sentences.zh: 这是一场票数非常接近的投票。

sentences.en: It's the tightest vote it's ever been.
sentences.zh: 这是有史以来票数最接近的一次。
比分是52比48。

sentences.en: But Clarence Thomas is confirmed as an associate justice of the United States Supreme Court, where he still sits 27 years later.
sentences.zh: 但克拉伦斯·托马斯被确认为美国最高法院联席大法官，27年后他依然在这个位置上。

sentences.en: During his time on the court, we rarely hear from Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 在他任职最高法院期间，我们很少听到克拉伦斯·托马斯发声。

sentences.en: Really long periods of years go by where Clarence Thomas does not ask a single question.
sentences.zh: 往往一连好几年过去，克拉伦斯·托马斯没有提出过一个问题。

sentences.en: He rarely writes opinions.
sentences.zh: 他很少撰写意见书。

sentences.en: But he has remained a very stalwart member of the court's conservative bloc.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然是最高法院保守派阵营中一位坚定的成员。

sentences.en: We don't hear a lot from Anita Hill, either, in the next couple of years.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，我们也没有听到太多关于安妮塔·希尔的消息。

sentences.en: But we do hear from American women.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实听到了美国女性的声音。

sentences.en: The message is simple.
sentences.zh: 信息很简单。

sentences.en: We want action now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在就要采取行动。

sentences.en: And the fact is, women have the power.
sentences.zh: 事实是，女性拥有权力。

sentences.en: Women have the votes.
sentences.zh: 女性拥有选票。

sentences.en: Women's ballots can make a fundamental change in this country and mobilize together determined women will do it.
sentences.zh: 女性的选票可以给这个国家带来根本性的改变，只要团结起来，坚定的女性就能做到这一点。

sentences.en: The next year is a presidential year.
sentences.zh: 接下来的一年是总统大选年。

sentences.en: Bill Clinton's running for president.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿正在竞选总统。

sentences.en: But it's also congressional elections.
sentences.zh: 但这也是国会选举年。

sentences.en: The events leading to Justice Thomas' confirmation, particularly Anita Hill's alleged harsh treatment by the all-male Senate Judiciary Committee,
sentences.zh: 导致托马斯大法官获得确认的事件，特别是安妮塔·希尔据称受到全男性参议院司法委员会严厉对待的事件，

sentences.en: ignited what some pundits have dubbed the year of the woman.
sentences.zh: 点燃了一些评论员所称的“女性之年”。

sentences.en: And when November 1992 comes and the results are in, the number of women in Congress has doubled.
sentences.zh: 当1992年11月到来且结果出炉时，国会中的女性人数翻了一番。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: So, Kate, here we are again, very similar circumstances 27 years later.
sentences.zh: 所以，凯特，我们又回到了这里，27年后情况惊人地相似。

sentences.en: And I think now the question is, how much has actually changed?
sentences.zh: 我认为现在的问题是，实际上改变了多少？

sentences.en: And if we get the same end result as last time, which was the confirmation of a Supreme Court justice accused of sexual misconduct,
sentences.zh: 如果我们得到和上次一样的最终结果，即确认了一位被指控性行为不端的最高法院大法官，

sentences.en: does that mean that not much has changed at all or not?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着其实并没有发生多大变化？

sentences.en: So let's start by talking about what's similar.
sentences.zh: 让我们从讨论相似之处开始。

sentences.en: So the most striking thing that's similar is who's on the committee now.
sentences.zh: 最显著的相似之处在于现在委员会里都有谁。

sentences.en: On the Republican side, we have two of the same men who were there in 1991 with Nia Hill.
sentences.zh: 在共和党阵营中，有两位曾在1991年与尼娅·希尔共事的男士依然在座。

sentences.en: And it's all white guys.
sentences.zh: 而且全都是白人男性。

sentences.en: It's all still all men, all white.
sentences.zh: 仍然全都是男性，全都是白人。

sentences.en: That's a very visual reminder of how much has not changed.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常直观的提醒，让人看到有多少事情没有改变。

sentences.en: And as in 1991, it's come down to a he said, she said situation.
sentences.zh: 正如1991年一样，这归结为一场各执一词的局面。

sentences.en: Once again, we have a credible woman making a credible charge and we have a respected jurist who's saying, really outraged, this is not something I would do.
sentences.zh: 我们再次看到一位可信的女性提出可信的指控，也看到一位受人尊敬的法官极其愤怒地表示，这不是我会做的事。

sentences.en: This is not something I have ever done in my life.
sentences.zh: 这不是我一生中做过的任何事。

sentences.en: So it's basically the same central dynamic.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是相同的核心动态。

sentences.en: She says it happened.
sentences.zh: 她说事情发生了。

sentences.en: She is 100 percent positive it did.
sentences.zh: 她百分之百确信发生了。

sentences.en: The accused, the nominee, is saying categorically it did not.
sentences.zh: 被指控者、被提名人则斩钉截铁地说没有。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对如此。

sentences.en: And she has been doubted a lot by the same Republicans who doubted Anita Hill.
sentences.zh: 而她受到了许多曾怀疑过安妮塔·希尔的共和党人的诸多怀疑。

sentences.en: So, for instance, you have Senator Hatch.
sentences.zh: 因此，举个例子，你有参议员哈奇。

sentences.en: Who was also Senator Hatch on the Judiciary Committee in 1991.
sentences.zh: 他也是1991年司法委员会的参议员哈奇。

sentences.en: Senator Hatch, same Senator Hatch.
sentences.zh: 参议员哈奇，还是那个参议员哈奇。

sentences.en: Now he's in his mid-80s.
sentences.zh: 现在他已经八十多岁了。

sentences.en: And he's saying, well, she seems to be mixed up.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，她似乎有些糊涂。

sentences.en: She seems to be mistaken.
sentences.zh: 她似乎记错了。

sentences.en: How much of what's different about this hearing do you think is because of an effort to make sure that this moment,
sentences.zh: 你认为这场听证会与众不同的地方，有多少是因为有人试图确保这个时刻——

sentences.en: the Kavanaugh-Blasey-Ford confrontation appears different or actually is different than the Hill-Thomas confrontation in 91.
sentences.zh: 即卡瓦诺与福特的对质，看起来或实际上不同于91年希尔与托马斯的对质。

sentences.en: In 1991, the senators on that panel had no idea this political wave that was going to move over them in next year's congressional elections, the year of the woman.
sentences.zh: 在1991年，那个委员会的参议员们完全没有料到，第二年的国会选举（即“女性之年”）将掀起一股政治浪潮，并席卷他们。

sentences.en: Now everyone is aware of those consequences.
sentences.zh: 现在大家都意识到这些后果了。

sentences.en: They are very aware that the American public is watching this.
sentences.zh: 他们非常清楚，美国公众正在注视着这一切。

sentences.en: And that if they do it wrong, there will be an electoral and a political and a social response to it.
sentences.zh: 而且如果他们搞砸了，将会引发选举、政治以及社会的强烈反弹。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it will be very quick and it will be very angry because women are already angry.
sentences.zh: 而且反应会非常迅速，非常愤怒，因为女性们已经满腔怒火了。

sentences.en: Women burned after Anita Hill.
sentences.zh: 经历过安妮塔·希尔事件后，女性们心如烈火。

sentences.en: Right now, they're already burning.
sentences.zh: 而现在，她们心中的怒火已经在燃烧了。

sentences.en: So, again, to look at what's different, just look at that room.
sentences.zh: 所以，再来看看有什么不同，只要看看那个房间就知道了。

sentences.en: The Republicans have said they're not going to ask questions.
sentences.zh: 共和党人已经表示他们不会亲自提问。

sentences.en: They're going to have an outside person, a woman, come in and ask questions.
sentences.zh: 他们将安排一个外部人员，一位女性来提问。

sentences.en: Dr. Blasey Ford has said she doesn't want an outside questioner.
sentences.zh: 福特博士曾表示她不希望有外部提问人。

sentences.en: She wants those senators.
sentences.zh: 她希望由那些参议员来问。

sentences.en: And Republicans said, well, you just want to do it so you'll have those same senators.
sentences.zh: 而共和党人则说，好吧，你这么做只是为了让那些老面孔参议员来质询。

sentences.en: You know, that's just political posturing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不过是政治姿态罢了。

sentences.en: Well, in some ways, the Republicans could also be accused of political posturing because they, too, do not want it seen that they had the same guys still sitting there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从某种程度上说，共和党人也可能被指责是在摆弄政治姿态，因为他们同样不想让人觉得还是原来那帮老家伙坐在那里。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 真耐人寻味。

sentences.en: So senators may say that this is a positive sign of this being different and that these times being different, that they're using an outsider.
sentences.zh: 因此，参议员们可能会说，使用外部人员是时代不同以及这件事具有积极意义的体现。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We aren't going to try to handle a sensitive interrogation like this on our own.
sentences.zh: 我们不打算独自处理这样一场敏感的质询。

sentences.en: We're bringing in an expert and a woman.
sentences.zh: 我们要引入一位专家，一位女性。

sentences.en: But, of course, the cynical interpretation of doing that is that they have eliminated the optics, which they know look bad.
sentences.zh: 但当然，对这一举动的讽刺性解读是，他们消除了那些他们心知肚明看起来很糟糕的视觉效果。

sentences.en: They've ensured the visual appearance of things is different, but perhaps not the more meaningful elements,
sentences.zh: 他们确保了表面上的视觉呈现有所不同，但或许更有意义的要素并没有变——

sentences.en: the perspectives of the senators involved and perhaps not the end result of it.
sentences.zh: 也就是涉事参议员的视角，以及最终的结果或许并未改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What they're saying is we are doing this to be sensitive.
sentences.zh: 他们的说辞是，我们这么做是为了展现关怀。

sentences.en: We understand so much how difficult it is to come forward.
sentences.zh: 我们非常理解站出来指认是多么困难的一件事。

sentences.en: We want to ensure that we are sensitive in our questioning.
sentences.zh: 我们要确保在提问时保持体恤与敏感。

sentences.en: But, of course, the response is, well, if anything has really changed, you would know how to be sensitive in your own questioning without having to outsource this.
sentences.zh: 但当然，外界的回应是，如果真有什么改变，你们本该懂得如何在不外包的情况下，用自己的提问展现出体恤。

sentences.en: So, Kate, let's talk about how this might end in the next couple of days or weeks and the significance of that.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯特，我们来聊聊这件事在接下来几天或几周内可能会如何收场，以及它的重要意义。

sentences.en: Obviously, it goes one of two ways.
sentences.zh: 很显然，结果无非两种。

sentences.en: Either Kavanaugh becomes a Supreme Court justice or he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 要么卡瓦诺成为最高法院大法官，要么他无法入选。

sentences.en: And it reminds me, actually, of the 2016 election and the intense symbolism of those outcomes for a lot of Americans.
sentences.zh: 这实际上让我想起了2016年大选，以及这些结果对于许多美国人所具有的强烈象征意义。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton wins and we are one version of this country.
sentences.zh: 希拉里获胜，我们就会成为另一种样子的国家。

sentences.en: Donald Trump wins and we're a very different version of this country, that it felt like a referendum on who we are.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普获胜，我们就会成为一个截然不同的国家，感觉就像是对我们究竟是谁的一次全民公投。

sentences.en: And it feels to me like that is happening all over again with Kavanaugh and Dr. Blasey Ford.
sentences.zh: 而在我看来，卡瓦诺和福特博士的事件正在让这一切重演。

sentences.en: If Kavanaugh is not confirmed, regardless of exactly why, the symbolism for many people will be that things have changed since Anita Hill, that things are different.
sentences.zh: 如果卡瓦诺没有通过确认，无论具体原因是什么，对许多人来说，其象征意义就是自安妮塔·希尔事件以来情况变了，一切都不同了。

sentences.en: And if Kavanaugh is confirmed, the symbolism is actually things haven't changed as much as we might have thought and as much as many people had hoped.
sentences.zh: 而如果卡瓦诺通过了确认，其象征意义实际上就是情况并没有我们想象的，也没有许多人所希望的那般改变了许多。

sentences.en: It's almost as if the country is on knife edge with this sort of self-image of ourselves trying to figure out which way it's going to go.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像是国家正处于刀刃之上，带着这种自我审视的形象，试图弄清楚究竟会走向何方。

sentences.en: I think it's a really scary moment for a lot of people because there's a certain amount of you go into this question cringing like you're not quite sure you want to see the outcome.
sentences.zh: 我认为对许多人来说这是一个非常可怕的时刻，因为你在面对这个问题时会不由自主地感到战战兢兢，有点不确定自己是否真的想看到结果。

sentences.en: You're not quite sure if you are those women who are still really feeling the loss of Hillary Clinton and feeling like that was a rejection of women trying to assert their voice and their authority.
sentences.zh: 你不太确定自己是否属于那些仍然深深感伤于希拉里·克林顿落败的女性，觉得那是对女性试图宣示自身声音和权威的一种排挤。

sentences.en: You kind of don't want to hear that all over again.
sentences.zh: 你甚至有点不想再次听到这些争论。

sentences.en: Obviously, it's a particular set of women.
sentences.zh: 很显然，这只针对特定的一群女性。

sentences.en: But I would say that if Brett Kavanaugh is confirmed, I would say that particular set of women is going to feel aggrieved all over again.
sentences.zh: 但我要说的是，如果布雷特·卡瓦诺通过了确认，这群特定的女性将会再次感到满腹委屈。

sentences.en: But aggrieved is almost too passive a term.
sentences.zh: 不过“委屈”这个词未免太被动了。

sentences.en: I think people are going to be really angry and they're going to see this as women not being taken seriously, women not being heard.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们会感到无比愤怒，并将此视为女性没有被认真对待、女性的声音没有被倾听的证明。

sentences.en: Like their attempt to speak out has been silenced.
sentences.zh: 就像她们发声的尝试被强行噤声了一样。

sentences.en: It really doesn't seem like there's a middle ground here.
sentences.zh: 这里似乎真的没有什么中间地带。

sentences.en: If Brett Kavanaugh doesn't get on the court, there are going to be all of his supporters and other people who think he was treated badly,
sentences.zh: 如果布雷特·卡瓦诺进不了最高法院，他的所有支持者以及其他认为他受到不公对待的人将会认为——

sentences.en: that this is political correctness run amok, that if someone can destroy a respected jurist like Brett Kavanaugh with an allegation from 36 years ago,
sentences.zh: 这是政治正确走向失控，如果仅凭一项36年前的指控就能毁掉一个备受尊敬的法官（如布雷特·卡瓦诺），

sentences.en: that any man can be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 那么任何男人都可以被毁掉。

sentences.en: And this isn't just a women versus men issue or divide on that knife edge.
sentences.zh: 在这个剑拔弩张的局面上，这不仅仅是女性与男性的对立或分歧。

sentences.en: It's many women, too, who think, oh, if my son were accused of this or if my husband was or if my brother was,
sentences.zh: 还有许多女性也在想：噢，如果我的儿子被指控了这一切，或者我的丈夫，或者我的兄弟，

sentences.en: he was run out because he was a conservative and someone like that can be taken down.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为他是个保守派就被逼入绝境，且这样的人能被轻易拉下马，

sentences.en: And this is the kind of country we have now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在生活的国家吗？

sentences.en: And that's not going to make them happy either.
sentences.zh: 这同样不会让他们感到高兴。

sentences.en: And I guess what's kind of terrifying about this situation is that these are just two people and that their stories and their lives are particular.
sentences.zh: 我想这种局势最可怕的地方在于，这仅仅涉及两个人，他们的故事和生活都是极其具体的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's going to come down to when Christine Blasey Ford comes into that room, what's her bearing at that table?
sentences.zh: 所以一切都将取决于克里斯蒂娜·布雷特·福特走进那个房间时，她在桌前的仪态如何？
zh_words: 克里斯蒂娜·布雷特·福特

sentences.en: How strong does her voice sound?
sentences.zh: 她的声音听起来有多坚定？

sentences.en: Does she seem credible?
sentences.zh: 她显得可信吗？

sentences.en: Does she seem believable?
sentences.zh: 她显得令人信服吗？

sentences.en: On the other side, Brett Kavanaugh, does he seem defensive?
sentences.zh: 而在另一边，布雷特·卡瓦诺，他显得防备心很重吗？

sentences.en: Does he seem too defensive?
sentences.zh: 他显得防御过头了吗？

sentences.en: Does he seem angry?
sentences.zh: 他显得很愤怒吗？

sentences.en: Is anger a good thing?
sentences.zh: 愤怒是一件好事吗？

sentences.en: Does that make him seem more outraged and therefore he's telling the truth?
sentences.zh: 这会让他显得更加愤慨，从而证明他在说实话吗？

sentences.en: Or does he come off like he's lying?
sentences.zh: 还是说他给人的感觉像是在撒谎？

sentences.en: It's all going to come down to these little details, not only from them, but it's also as much as these might be senators asking questions, they too are ordinary people.
sentences.zh: 一切都将归结于这些微小的细节，不仅取决于他们两人，而且，尽管这些参议员们是在提问，但他们同样也是普通人。

sentences.en: And it's going to be how they filter it as ordinary people, what they're seeing.
sentences.zh: 这一切将取决于他们作为普通人如何去过滤和看待他们所看到的一切。

sentences.en: But the symbolism of the end result will probably not account for all of that.
sentences.zh: 但最终结果的象征意义可能无法完全涵盖所有这些细节。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the end, it's going to be how much has this country changed and how much have we not.
sentences.zh: 到头来，关键在于这个国家究竟改变了多少，而我们又在哪些方面停滞不前。

sentences.en: Kate, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 凯特，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Republicans on the Senate Judiciary Committee said they had selected a female lawyer to question Dr. Blasey and Judge Kavanaugh at Thursday's hearing.
sentences.zh: 周二，参议院司法委员会的共和党人表示，他们已经挑选了一名女律师，在周四的听证会上质询福特博士和卡瓦诺法官。

sentences.en: The lawyer will ask questions on behalf of the Republican senators, while Senate Democrats will do their own questioning.
sentences.zh: 这名律师将代表共和党参议员提问，而民主党参议员则会进行他们自己的质询。

sentences.en: In explaining the Republicans' decision, the committee's chairman, Senator Chuck Grassley, who was on the Judiciary Committee in 1991, said, quote,
sentences.zh: 在解释共和党人的决定时，曾于1991年任职于司法委员会的委员会主席、参议员查克·格拉斯利表示，原话是——

sentences.en: quote, we've done it because we want to depoliticize the whole process, like the Democrats politicized the Anita Hill thing.
sentences.zh: “我们这么做是因为我们希望将整个过程去政治化，就像民主党人把安妮塔·希尔事件政治化那样。”

sentences.en: Later on Tuesday, Grassley announced that the committee had scheduled a vote on Judge Kavanaugh's confirmation to the Supreme Court for Friday, the morning after the hearing.
sentences.zh: 周二晚些时候，格拉斯利宣布，委员会已安排在听证会结束后的次日周五上午，对卡瓦诺法官最高法院大法官的提名进行投票。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: And now a new charge comes up.
sentences.zh: 现在又出现了一项新的指控。

sentences.en: And she said, well, it might not be him, and there were gaps, and she said she was totally inebriated, and she was all messed up.
sentences.zh: 她说，嗯，可能不是他，其中有记忆断层，她还说自己当时完全喝醉了，整个人一团糟。

sentences.en: And she doesn't know it was him, but it might have been him.
sentences.zh: 她不知道是不是他，但也有可能是他。

sentences.en: Oh, gee, let's not make him a Supreme Court judge because of that.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，我们可别因为这个就不让他当最高法院大法官吧。

sentences.en: During a news conference at the United Nations, President Trump attacked the second woman to come forward with allegations against Judge Kavanaugh, calling her claims unreliable.
sentences.zh: 在联合国的一场新闻发布会上，特朗普总统抨击了第二位站出来指控卡瓦诺法官的女性，称她的指控不可信。

sentences.en: The woman, Deborah Ramirez, told The New Yorker that during a night of heavy drinking their freshman year at Yale, Kavanaugh exposed himself to her at a party.
sentences.zh: 这名叫黛博拉·拉米雷斯的女性告诉《纽约客》，在耶鲁大学大一那年的一晚狂饮之后，卡瓦诺在一次聚会上向她露出了下体。

sentences.en: The Democrats are playing a con game, C-O-N, a con game.
sentences.zh: 民主党人在玩骗局，骗局，这是一场骗局。

sentences.en: And they know it's a con game.
sentences.zh: 而且他们心知肚明这是一场骗局。

sentences.en: They know he's high quality.
sentences.zh: 他们知道他素质极高。

sentences.en: And they weaken each other.
sentences.zh: 而他们却在互相削弱。

sentences.en: They're weakening.
sentences.zh: 他们正在变弱。

sentences.en: They know it's a con game.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这是一场骗局。

sentences.en: Go ahead.
sentences.zh: 说吧。

sentences.en: And.
sentences.zh: 还有。

sentences.en: This is a very important day.
sentences.zh: 这是非常重要的一天。

sentences.en: Judgment Day has come.
sentences.zh: 审判日已经到来。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Bill Cosby was sentenced to three to ten years in prison for drugging and sexually assaulting a woman at his Pennsylvania home 14 years ago.
sentences.zh: 周二，比尔·科斯比因14年前在宾夕法尼亚州的家中下药并性侵一名女性，被判处三到十年监禁。

sentences.en: Cosby had been convicted in April of assaulting the woman, Andrea Constand, who had thought of him as a mentor,
sentences.zh: 科斯比于4月份被判性侵罪名成立，受害人安德烈娅·康斯坦曾将他视为人生导师，

sentences.en: but ended up being one of the dozens of women who have accused him of sexual abuse.
sentences.zh: 但最终却成为了指控他性虐待的数十名女性之一。

sentences.en: Nine of those women, along with Constand, were in the courthouse when Cosby was sentenced.
sentences.zh: 宣判时，包括康斯坦在内的其中九名女性来到了法院。

sentences.en: And I'm happy that the judge sentenced Bill Cosby accordingly.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴法官对比尔·科斯比作出了相应的判决。

sentences.en: And I'm grateful to Andrea for standing strong.
sentences.zh: 我也很感激安德烈娅坚强地挺了过来。

sentences.en: Moments after the sentencing, Cosby, who was once described as America's dad from his days as Dr. Huxtable on The Cosby Show, was escorted to prison in handcuffs.
sentences.zh: 宣判后不久，这位曾因在《科斯比一家》中饰演赫克斯塔布尔博士而被誉为“美国老爹”的科斯比，戴着手铐被押送进了监狱。

sentences.en: Mr. Cosby, any comments, sir?
sentences.zh: 科斯比先生，有什么想说的吗，先生？

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日简报》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为您盘点如何为假期接待亲友做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人在您家宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种对光线极度敏感、一关灯就能睡着的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会喝断片来助眠。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们睡觉时需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏史或饮食禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约客》应用上或在您喜欢的任何播客平台上找到《Wirecutter秀》。
